lines.japanese: 「ほら、パン焼けたぞ」
lines.english: “Here. Toast’s ready.”
“Mm…”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁぁ…」
lines.english: “Haaah…”

lines.japanese: 「寝不足か？」
lines.english: “Didn’t sleep enough?”

lines.japanese:
「ちょっとな…
さっきまでメール処理してたから」
lines.english: “A little… I was answering emails until just now.”

lines.japanese: 公約通り、浜田さんはしっかり雑務をｚｉｐでくれた。
lines.english: True to his word, Hamada had sent me a fat ZIP file full of busywork.

lines.japanese:
「家に仕事持ち帰ってんのかよ…
典型的な日本のサラリーマンだなお前。
いつか過労死するぞ」
lines.english: “You bring work home too? You’re the perfect Japanese salaryman. You’ll work yourself to death one day.”

lines.japanese: 「…否定はしないけどな」
lines.english: “…I can’t deny that.”

lines.japanese:
解凍した後のファイル数を見て、
軽くめまいに襲われた時に眠っておけばよかった。
lines.english: When I saw the number of files in the archive and felt the first wave of dizziness, I should have gone to bed.

lines.japanese:
「そうやって身を粉にして働いて、
家族養うだけで自分を犠牲にする人生か。
生きてて何が楽しいんだか」
lines.english: “So you grind yourself down, sacrifice your whole life, and do nothing but support your family. Where’s the pleasure in living like that?”

lines.japanese: けど、こいつに言われたくないって気持ちはある。
lines.english: Coming from her, that was rich.

lines.japanese:
何しろ俺が真夜中に仕事に手をつけるほど
眠れなくなってしまった原因は…
lines.english: After all, the reason I had been unable to sleep and finally started working in the middle of the night was…

lines.japanese:
「家族が本当に大切だったら、
そのために頑張れるのは楽しいことだと思うぞ。
まだ経験で語れないけど」
lines.english: “If you really care about your family, working hard for them is its own kind of happiness. Not that I can speak from experience yet.”

lines.japanese:
「あ～、そりゃそうだろうな。
何しろお前の家族になってやろうって相手は…」
lines.english: “Oh, I’m sure. Especially when the woman offering to become your family is—”

lines.japanese: 「………ほら、目玉焼き」
lines.english: “…Here. Fried egg.”
“Mm.”

lines.japanese:
かずさの方も、俺が言葉を遮った意図を理解したのか、
それ以上は嫌味ったらしく踏み込んでこなかった。
lines.english: Kazusa understood why I had cut her off and, for once, chose not to press the barb any deeper.

lines.japanese: 「塩コショウ？　ソース？　醤油？」
lines.english: “Salt and pepper? Worcestershire sauce? Soy sauce?”

lines.japanese: 「ケチャップ」
lines.english: “Ketchup.”

lines.japanese: 「調味料まで甘めのものを…」
lines.english: “Even your condiments have to be sweet…”

lines.japanese: 「あたしの勝手だ」
lines.english: “My choice.”

lines.japanese:
鍋、フライパン、皿、スプーン、ナイフとフォーク、箸。
オーブントースターにパンに卵に生野菜に調味料。
lines.english: A pot, a frying pan, plates, spoons, knives and forks, chopsticks. A toaster oven, bread, eggs, raw vegetables, and condiments.

lines.japanese:
たった一日で、
かずさの部屋には結構な家財道具が入り込んだ。
…とはいえ全部俺の部屋からの輸入品だけど。
lines.english: In a single day, Kazusa’s apartment had acquired a respectable quantity of household goods—though every last one had been imported from mine.

lines.japanese: 「さてと、それじゃいただきます」
lines.english: “All right, then. Thanks for the food.”
“Mm…”
“…” I gave her a pointed look.

lines.japanese: 「…いただきます」
lines.english: “…Thanks for the food.”

lines.japanese: 「食べてよし」
lines.english: “Now you may eat.”

lines.japanese: 「っとに、鬱陶しい」
lines.english: “God, you’re annoying.”

lines.japanese:
昨日もしつこく言い聞かせたのに…
って、絶対にわざと反抗してるよな、こいつ。
lines.english: I had drilled it into her yesterday. At this point, she had to be defying me on purpose.

lines.japanese:
「って、お前そんなにジャム塗るな。
また一瓶空けるつもりか」
lines.english: “Hey, don’t put that much jam on. Are you planning to finish another whole jar?”

lines.japanese:
「朝に甘いものは重要だろ。
糖分取らないと頭働かないぞ」
lines.english: “Sugar is important in the morning. Your brain won’t work without it.”

lines.japanese: 「それにしても限度が…って、紅茶にも入れるのかよ！」
lines.english: “There are still limits. Wait—you’re putting it in your tea too?”

lines.japanese: 「ロシアンティーも知らないのか日本人は」
lines.english: “Haven’t you Japanese ever heard of Russian tea?”

lines.japanese:
…まぁ、こっちのパラノイア的甘党に関しては、
わざとでも何でもないことは歴史が証明済みだけど。
lines.english: Though history had already proved that her deranged devotion to sweets, unlike her refusal to say thanks, was entirely sincere.

lines.japanese:
「へぇ、しばらくは出張扱いなのか。
思ったより気楽なんだな、お前の仕事も」
lines.english: “So you’re officially out in the field for a while. Your job’s easier than I thought.”

lines.japanese:
「言っておくが仕事量は減ってないからな。
むしろこの取材分だけ増えてる」
lines.english: “The workload hasn’t gone down. This feature has simply been added to everything else.”

lines.japanese:
かずさは味がわかってるのか怪しいくらい
素早く朝食を平らげ、
今は二杯目のロシアンティーを喉に流し込んでいる。
lines.english: Kazusa had demolished breakfast too quickly to have tasted any of it and was now pouring a second cup of Russian tea down her throat.

lines.japanese:
今日もまた新品のジャムが一瓶消えた。
…駄目だこいつ。早く食生活改善させないと。
lines.english: Another brand-new jar of jam was already gone. This was hopeless. I needed to do something about her diet, fast.

lines.japanese:
「そっちはどうなんだ？
今日は練習か？」
lines.english: “What about you? Practice today?”

lines.japanese: 「毎日練習だ、朝の１０時から」
lines.english: “Every day. Starting at ten.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちでも一日十時間なのか？」
lines.english: “Ten hours a day here too?”

lines.japanese: 「お前のせいでな」
lines.english: “Because of you.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか…」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese:
その決めつけは、そりゃ嬉しいけど、
結構苦しくもあるんだけどな。
lines.english: Having her pin it all on me made me happy, of course. It also hurt quite a bit.

lines.japanese:
「で、これがコンサートやコンクールの直前だと、
寝て食べる以外の時間は全部弾いてる」
lines.english: “Right before a concert or competition, I play every minute I’m not eating or asleep.”

lines.japanese: 「…人間のやることじゃないよな」
lines.english: “…That hardly sounds human.”

lines.japanese:
「演奏家なんてみんなそんなもんだ。
あたしだけ特別こんなことやってる訳じゃない」
lines.english: “All performers do it. I’m not putting myself through anything special.”

lines.japanese: 「大変なんだな…」
lines.english: “That’s a hard life…”

lines.japanese:
「そうだよ。だから家事とか私生活のことなんか
何もできなくて当然なんだ。
する暇がないからな」
lines.english: “Exactly. So of course I can’t keep house or deal with any of that everyday stuff. I don’t have time.”

lines.japanese:
「お前は単に物臭なだけだろ。
ピアノやってなかった頃だって全然…」
lines.english: “You’re just lazy. Even when you weren’t playing the piano, you never—”

lines.japanese:
「うるさいな。
あの頃のあたしは親に反抗してたからだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Back then I was rebelling against my mother.”

lines.japanese: 「カッコ悪かったもんなぁ、あの頃のお前…」
lines.english: “You were pretty lame back then.”

lines.japanese: 「お前は今もカッコ悪いけどな」
lines.english: “You’re still lame now.”

lines.japanese: 「まぁな」
lines.english: “True.”

lines.japanese:
それでもその立ち振る舞いが、
憧れてしまうくらいカッコ良かったのが、
またタチが悪かったんだけど。
lines.english: The trouble was that even then, the way she carried herself was so cool I couldn’t help admiring her.

lines.japanese:
「さてと、それじゃ練習に行くか。
お前はどうするんだ？
あたしにしつこく付きまとうのか？」
lines.english: “Well, time to practice. What about you? Planning to follow me around like a pest?”

lines.japanese:
そして今、親への反抗をやめて、
ストイックな音楽家になった冬馬かずさは、
結局、何をしてもカッコ良いってことを証明した。
lines.english: Now that she’d stopped rebelling and become a disciplined musician, Kazusa Touma had proved she could make anything look cool.

lines.japanese:
俺の作った食事を感謝もせず食べてても、
俺が世話を焼くのを当然のように受け止めてても、
俺にどれだけ悪態をついてても…
lines.english: Even when she ate my food without a word of gratitude. Even when she accepted my care as her due. Even when she hurled abuse at me…

lines.japanese:
「なぁ、かずさ。
今日の練習、昼からにできないか？」
lines.english: “Hey, Kazusa. Could you put off practice until this afternoon?”

lines.japanese: 「…なんでだよ？」
lines.english: “…Why?”

lines.japanese: 「午前中、俺に付き合ってくれ」
lines.english: “Spend the morning with me.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「駄目か…？」
lines.english: “Would that be so bad…?”

lines.japanese:
「お、お前、何言ってんだよ。
そんなこと、今さら…」
lines.english: “W-what are you talking about? After all this time, how can you—”

lines.japanese:
「けどお前、家財道具揃えないと。
空っぽの部屋のまま、一月過ごすつもりなのか？」
lines.english: “You need furniture and appliances. Were you planning to spend the month in an empty apartment?”

lines.japanese:
「プリンもアイスクリームも、
今のままじゃ食べたいときに食べられないぞ。
それでもいいんだな？」
lines.english: “As things stand, you won’t be able to eat pudding or ice cream whenever you want. Are you prepared to live with that?”

lines.japanese:
だから、自分の照れ隠しのために、
かずさのカッコ良さを崩そうと躍起になり。
lines.english: Embarrassed by my own feelings, I threw myself into knocking Kazusa off her pedestal.

lines.japanese:
…そのせいで、
かずさが普段見せない一面を引き出してしまい、
余計にヤバい気持ちになってしまう。
lines.english: That only brought out a side of her she rarely showed, making those feelings all the more dangerous.

lines.japanese:
またしても悪循環。
ほんと、学習しないな、俺も。
lines.english: The same vicious circle again. I never learned.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ、間に合った」
lines.english: “Whew. We made it.”

lines.japanese:
「一本遅らせてもいいから全力で走るな。
またヒール折るぞ？」
lines.english: “Better to miss one train than run flat out. You’ll break another heel.”

lines.japanese:
「…嫌なことを思い出させるな春希は。
あの時は雪だったから仕方ないんだって」
lines.english: “…You just had to bring that up, didn’t you, Haruki? It was snowing. I couldn’t help it.”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく、お前は今怪我していい訳ないんだから、
もうちょっと慎重にだな………あ」
lines.english: “In any case, you can’t afford an injury now. You need to be more caref—oh.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、そんなヘマなんかしないって言ってるだろ。
コンサートが近づくと、集中力が増してくるから」
lines.english: “I told you, I’m not going to make a stupid mistake like that. I get more focused as a concert approaches.”

lines.japanese:
「これが三日前くらいになると、
自分で言うのもなんだけど凄いぞ。
１００メートル先で誰かが石を蹴った音が聞こえたり…」
lines.english: “Once I’m about three days out from a concert, that focus becomes almost superhuman, if I do say so myself. I can hear someone kick a pebble a hundred meters away…”
“…Haruki?”

lines.japanese: なんて、こった。
lines.english: Oh, hell.

lines.japanese: 「かずさ…」
lines.english: “Kazusa…”

lines.japanese:
「え、なに………きゃっ！？
お、お、おい…っ」
lines.english: “What are you—ah! H-hey!”

lines.japanese:
かずさの肩に手を置くと、
力を込めてくるりと半回転。
lines.english: I placed my hands on her shoulders and spun her firmly halfway around.

lines.japanese:
そのままドアの方を向かせ、
背中から抱きしめるように身体を重ねる。
lines.english: Turning her toward the train door, I pressed myself against her back, almost as though I were embracing her from behind.

lines.japanese:
「は、春希…
いきなり、なにすんだよお前…っ」
lines.english: “H-Haruki… what the hell are you doing all of a sudden?”

lines.japanese:
俺の、そんな強引にも程がある行為に、
かずさが全身を思いっきり強ばらせる。
lines.english: At the sudden manhandling, Kazusa’s whole body went rigid.

lines.japanese: 「あんま喋るな…」
lines.english: “Try not to talk…”

lines.japanese:
「なんで、なんで…
お前、こんなことしたらどうなるか…」
lines.english: “Why? Why are you—do you know what’ll happen if you do this?”

lines.japanese:
「頼む、目立たないでくれ…
昨日言ったことがもう現実になってる」
lines.english: “Please, don’t draw attention. What I warned you about yesterday has already come true.”

lines.japanese: 「…何のことだ？」
lines.english: “…What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「広告にお前の写真が…」
lines.english: “There’s a picture of you in that ad…”

lines.japanese: 「…んだってぇ？」
lines.english: “…What did you say?”

lines.japanese:
かずさに説教を垂れつつふと見上げた先の、
お馴染みの写真週刊誌の中吊り広告。
lines.english: While lecturing Kazusa, I happened to look up at an overhead ad for one of those familiar weekly tabloids.

lines.japanese:
前から三番目の記事紹介に
『冬馬かずさ』の文字と顔写真を見た瞬間、
俺の心拍数は一気に３０近く上がった。
lines.english: The instant I saw the name “Kazusa Touma” and her photograph beside the third teaser from the top, my heart rate jumped by nearly thirty beats per minute.

lines.japanese:
「とにかく下りるまでずっと外見てろ。
絶対こっち向くなよ？」
lines.english: “Face the window until we get off. Whatever you do, don’t turn around.”

lines.japanese: 「けど、どんなこと書いてあるか…」
lines.english: “But I want to see what they wrote…”

lines.japanese:
「見るな。
デタラメばっかりだ」
lines.english: “Don’t. It’s all lies.”

lines.japanese:
その一言で、
かずさにはその記事の内容が、
もしかしたら伝わってしまったかもしれない。
lines.english: That alone may have told her exactly what kind of article it was.

lines.japanese:
けど、やっぱ駄目だ。
こんな…
lines.english: But no. I couldn’t let her see this.

lines.japanese: 『取材拒否　暴言乱発　ファンの声援も無視』
lines.english: “REFUSES INTERVIEWS—HURLS ABUSE—IGNORES CHEERING FANS”

lines.japanese:
『初来日・天才二世ピアニスト冬馬かずさ
母親譲りの唯我独尊』
lines.english: “SECOND-GENERATION PIANO PRODIGY KAZUSA TOUMA MAKES HER FIRST VISIT TO JAPAN—HER MOTHER’S ARROGANCE LIVES ON”

lines.japanese:
“これぞ三流週刊誌”という表現が
気持ちいいくらいぴったりハマる、
お馴染みの見出し。
lines.english: A textbook tabloid headline. The phrase “third-rate weekly rag” fit almost too perfectly.

lines.japanese:
「考え過ぎかもしれないけど、
誰かがお前の正体に気づくかもしれない。
…そんなことになったらヤだろ？」
lines.english: “I may be worrying too much, but someone could recognize you. You wouldn’t want that, would you?”

lines.japanese: 「春希…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
本当は『気づかれたくない』より
『見せたくない』気持ちの方が強かったけど、
いちいちそんな心情を説明する必要なんかない。
lines.english: In truth, it wasn’t so much that I didn’t want anyone to recognize her. I simply didn’t want her to see it. But I had no reason to explain every feeling in my heart.

lines.japanese:
ただ、俺がこうしないと。
かずさと日本との間の、緩衝材にならないと…
lines.english: I had to do this. I had to be the buffer between Kazusa and Japan…

lines.japanese:
「だから、悪い。
ちょっと窮屈かもしれないけど…」
lines.english: “So I’m sorry. I know it’s cramped, but…”

lines.japanese:
「窮屈だ。悪い。最悪だ。
お前は本当に厚かましい奴だ」
lines.english: “It’s cramped. It’s awful. It’s the worst. You really have no shame.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんな…」
lines.english: “Sorry…”

lines.japanese:
「謝れば済むと思ってやがる。
あたしなら、許すだろうって思ってやがる」
lines.english: “You think saying sorry makes everything all right. You think that because it’s me, I’ll forgive you.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは…」
lines.english: “I don’t…”

lines.japanese: 「………ふざけるな」
lines.english: “…Go to hell.”

lines.japanese:
口からの罵詈雑言はそのままだったけど、
それでも俺は、かずさが落ち着いたことを知り、
少しだけ胸をなで下ろした。
lines.english: The abuse kept coming, but I could feel the tension leaving Kazusa, and at last I let myself breathe.

lines.japanese:
だって、全身の緊張が解けたから。
少しだけ、俺の体が触れるのを許し始めたから。
lines.english: Her whole body had relaxed. Just a little, she seemed willing to let me stay pressed against her.

lines.japanese: 車内は、いつも通りだった。
lines.english: The train car was just as it always was.

lines.japanese:
皆、目の前の写真に写ってる女性と、
ドアに不自然にへばりついてる女性との
相関関係には気づいていなかった。
lines.english: No one seemed to notice any connection between the woman in the photograph before them and the woman clinging unnaturally to the door.

lines.japanese:
その事実に俺の判断が効いたのかどうかは
正直よくわからなかったけど、
でも、今後もこういう判断が発生することだけは実感した。
lines.english: Honestly, I had no idea whether my intervention had helped. I did know this wouldn’t be the last time I had to make a call like that.

lines.japanese: 「はぁ…」
lines.english: “Haaah…”
“Ngh…!”

lines.japanese: 『このままじゃ、多分そのうちボロボロになる』
lines.english: “Sooner or later, she’s going to fall apart.”

lines.japanese:
曜子さんの言ってたことは杞憂だと思ってたけど、
実はあまりそうでないのかも…
lines.english: I had thought Youko was worrying over nothing. Maybe she had a point.

lines.japanese: やっぱり…俺が守らなくちゃならないのか？
lines.english: Did I really have to protect her?

lines.japanese:
俺のささやかな未来のためには、
一番遠ざけなくちゃならないこの女を…？
lines.english: This woman whom, for the sake of my modest little future, I ought to keep farther away than anyone?

lines.japanese: 「…なぁ、春希」
lines.english: “…Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「…なんだよ、かずさ？」
lines.english: “…What is it, Kazusa?”

lines.japanese:
「さっきからなんか当たってるぞ？
…あたしのお尻に」
lines.english: “Something’s been pressing against me for a while. Against my ass.”

lines.japanese: 「カメラだよ！」
lines.english: “It’s the camera!”

lines.japanese:
「ほら…
こんな感じですけど、いかがでしょう？」
lines.english: “There you go. What do you think?”

lines.japanese: 「へぇ…」
lines.english: “Wow…”

lines.japanese:
「へ、へぇじゃない！
鏡、鏡はどこだ！」
lines.english: “Don’t just say wow! Where’s a mirror?”

lines.japanese:
「大丈夫ですよ。
ほんとお似合いです」
lines.english: “Don’t worry. It really suits you.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな感想はいいから、早く！」
lines.english: “I don’t need your opinion. Find me a mirror!”

lines.japanese: 「慌てるなよ…」
lines.english: “Calm down…”

lines.japanese:
「慌てるに決まってるだろ！
こんな、こんな…」
lines.english: “Of course I won’t calm down! This is—this is…”

lines.japanese: 「な…っ」
lines.english: “What…?”

lines.japanese:
「彼女、髪長くて綺麗だから、
ちょっと勿体ないかなって気もしたけど、
こっちもいけますね～」
lines.english: “Her hair is so long and beautiful that it seemed a shame to put it up, but this look really works too.”

lines.japanese: 「本当だ…全然ＯＫですね」
lines.english: “You’re right… It totally works.”
“Y-you—you…”

lines.japanese:
電車から降りて俺たちが最初に目指したのは、
家電量販店でも家具店でもなく、
アクセサリショップだった。
lines.english: The first place we visited after leaving the train was neither an electronics store nor a furniture shop, but an accessories boutique.

lines.japanese:
そこで、結構お馴染みになった店員に相談し、
『素顔が気取られないグッズ』という、
あまりに怪しい条件で見繕ってもらったのがこれ。
lines.english: There, I consulted a clerk I knew fairly well by now and asked her to find us “something that keeps people from recognizing your face”—an alarmingly suspicious request that produced this result.

lines.japanese:
コームの髪飾りで髪をサイドアップにまとめ、
伊達眼鏡で目を隠し…
lines.english: A decorative comb swept Kazusa’s hair up at one side, while a pair of clear-lensed glasses obscured her eyes.

lines.japanese:
これで『ただ今話題沸騰のピアニスト冬馬かずさ』改め、
『その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん』の出来上がり。
lines.english: And just like that, “Kazusa Touma, the pianist everyone is talking about” became “that pretty woman in glasses you might see anywhere.”

lines.japanese:
「…何だこれは？
馬鹿にしてるのかお前」
lines.english: “…What have you done to me? Is this some kind of joke?”

lines.japanese:
「え～？
すごく似合ってますよねぇ？」
lines.english: “What? It looks wonderful on you, doesn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「ねぇ？」
lines.english: “Doesn’t it?”

lines.japanese: ………出来上がり、だよな？
lines.english: That completed the disguise… right?

lines.japanese:
「女の髪や顔を勝手にいじるなんて、
お前もえらくなったもんだよなぁ…
五年前は岩石よりも堅い委員長だったのに」
lines.english: “Messing with a woman’s hair and face without asking… You’ve certainly come a long way. Five years ago, you were a class rep with all the flexibility of a boulder.”

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないだろ。
素のままで歩けなくなったお前が悪い」
lines.english: “What choice did I have? It’s your fault you can’t go around as yourself anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「っ、あたしのせいじゃない！」
lines.english: “That isn’t my fault!”

lines.japanese:
「うん、お前の責任じゃなくてお前の実力だよ。
…別に卑下することなんかない」
lines.english: “Right. It isn’t your fault—it’s a testament to your talent. There’s no reason to put yourself down.”

lines.japanese:
俺がこんな手を思いついたヒントは、
付属時代、俺と知り合う前の、放課後の雪菜だった。
lines.english: The idea came from the way Setsuna used to look after school at Houjou High, before we knew each other.

lines.japanese:
眼鏡をかけて三つ編みにして、わざと野暮ったい服を着て、
学園のアイドルという自分を、学園近くのスーパーで、
二年半も隠蔽し続けた嘘つきな女の子。
lines.english: For two and a half years, that little liar had worked at the supermarket near campus in glasses, braids, and deliberately dowdy clothes, hiding the fact that she was the most popular girl in school.

lines.japanese:
…その手法をあろうことか、かずさに施すって、
俺って結構酷い奴なのかもしれないけど。
lines.english: Adapting that method for Kazusa of all people might have made me a fairly terrible person.

lines.japanese:
でも今は、背に腹を替えられない。
普段のかずさを世間の目から逸らすことが何よりも先決だ。
lines.english: But necessity left no room for scruples. Above all, I had to keep the public from seeing Kazusa as she normally looked.

lines.japanese:
「どうします？
別の持ってきましょうか？」
lines.english: “What would you like to do? Shall I bring something different?”

lines.japanese:
「だとさ。
どうする？」
lines.english: “You heard her. What do you want?”

lines.japanese:
「…会計お願いします。
両方とも」
lines.english: “…We’ll take them. Both.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、お買いあげありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Certainly. Thank you.”

lines.japanese:
そのふてくされた沈黙は、
『どれでも同じだ馬鹿野郎』という台詞を、
しっかりと表情で語っていた。
lines.english: Her sulky silence clearly said, “They’re all the same, asshole.”

lines.japanese:
「言っておくけど、
こんなもの買ったって明日から使わないぞ？」
lines.english: “I’m warning you now: buying this stuff doesn’t mean I’m wearing it tomorrow.”

lines.japanese:
その後、追加でマフラーと帽子も揃え、
『その辺にいる眼鏡の綺麗なお姉さん』から、
『その辺にいる重装備の綺麗なお姉さん』に早変わり。
lines.english: We added a scarf and hat afterward, transforming “the pretty woman in glasses you might see anywhere” into “the pretty woman in full winter armor you might see anywhere.”

lines.japanese: …なんか違うような気もするけど。
lines.english: Something about that seemed to miss the point.

lines.japanese:
「何でそんなに嫌がるんだよ？
そりゃ、少し窮屈かもしれないけど、
街でいきなり正体バレするよりは…」
lines.english: “Why do you hate it so much? It may be a little uncomfortable, but surely that’s better than being recognized in the street.”

lines.japanese: 「あたし、髪結べないんだ」
lines.english: “I don’t know how to put my hair up.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「絶対にグシャグシャになるんだ。
…前に一度試して、母さんに呆れられたんだ」
lines.english: “It always turns into a complete mess. I tried once, and even Mom was appalled.”

lines.japanese: こいつが昔からずっとストレートロングのままなのは…
lines.english: So that was why she had worn her hair long and straight all these years.

lines.japanese:
「だから、その…
眼鏡は使うけど、コームの方は…」
lines.english: “So, well… I’ll wear the glasses, but the comb…”

lines.japanese: 「俺が結べばいいんだろ？」
lines.english: “I’ll do your hair.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
髪をひっつめることすら満足にできない、
天才的に手先が器用なはずのピアニスト。
lines.english: A pianist with genius in her fingers, yet unable even to put up her own hair.

lines.japanese:
それは多分、生来のめんどくさがりな性格が
多分に影響してるとは思うけれど。
lines.english: Her natural laziness probably had a great deal to do with that.

lines.japanese:
「このまとめ方なら、さっきのやり方見てたから、
ちゃんと再現できると思う」
lines.english: “I watched how the clerk did it just now. I can do it the same way.”

lines.japanese:
髪をまとめるのと、
綺麗なストレートのままにしておくのと、
どっちが大変なんだよと思わないでもないけれど。
lines.english: I couldn’t help wondering which was really harder: putting her hair up or keeping it so beautifully straight.

lines.japanese: 「けどそれって、毎朝…」
lines.english: “But that means every morning…”

lines.japanese: 「迷惑か？」
lines.english: “Would that bother you?”

lines.japanese:
でも、こいつができないって言うならしょうがない。
独占取材の邪魔になりそうな要素は、
担当の俺が極力排除するしかないから。
lines.english: If she said she couldn’t manage it herself, then I had no choice. I was the reporter responsible for this exclusive, so it was up to me to eliminate anything that might get in the way.

lines.japanese:
「こっちの仕事の都合もあるから、
朝早くでないと無理な日もあると思う。
だから、できれば生活リズムを合わせてくれると…」
lines.english: “Some days my work may mean I have to come by first thing in the morning. So if possible, I’d like you to keep roughly the same hours I do…”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱ、駄目か？」
lines.english: “Is that no good?”

lines.japanese:
「知るか。
勝手にしろ」
lines.english: “Whatever. Do what you want.”

lines.japanese:
なんて、いつも通り悪態をつきながら、
『勝手にしろ』というお墨付きとともに、
その意を悟られまいと、さっさと先に歩き出す。
lines.english: As always, she hid her consent inside an insult, then hurried ahead before I could read anything more into “do what you want.”

lines.japanese:
結局、かずさは散々文句を垂れまくっても、
何だかんだでこっちの主張を受け入れてくれる、
最後の砦的な優しさを失いはしない。
lines.english: For all her bitter complaints, there was one last kindness Kazusa never lost: in the end, she would accept what I was asking of her.

lines.japanese:
俺の前では、いつもいつもふてくされてて、
俺の干渉をとても迷惑そうに受け流して、
けれど気がつくと隣にいたりして…
lines.english: With me, she was always sulking, always treating my interference as an intolerable nuisance—and yet, whenever I looked, there she was beside me.

lines.japanese:
今のかずさは、
まるで俺と雪菜が出逢う前の…
lines.english: The Kazusa I was seeing now was almost the girl she’d been before Setsuna and I ever met…

lines.japanese:
「そうだ…
かずさ、ちょっと待ってくれ」
lines.english: “Oh, right… Kazusa, wait a second.”

lines.japanese:
「なんでだよ？
早いところ他の買い物も済ませないと、
練習時間がどんどん削られて…」
lines.english: “Why? If we don’t hurry and finish the rest of the shopping, you’ll keep eating into my practice time…”

lines.japanese:
「一枚だけ、一枚！
ほら、そこに立って」
lines.english: “Just one picture. One! Stand over there.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
言いながら、俺がカメラをケースから取り出すと、
眼鏡越しのかずさの瞳が、ちょっと揺らぐ。
lines.english: As I spoke, I pulled the camera from its case, and Kazusa’s eyes wavered behind the glasses.

lines.japanese:
「ほら、笑って…
って、普段通りの方がいいか。
ほらかずさ、しかめっ面頼む」
lines.english: “Come on, smile… No, perhaps your normal face would be better. Give me a scowl, Kazusa.”

lines.japanese: 「…やっぱりあたしを馬鹿にしてるだろ、お前」
lines.english: “…You are making fun of me.”

lines.japanese:
「そう、そんな感じ…
行きます、はい…っ」
lines.english: “That’s it… Here we go…”

lines.japanese: 「っ…あ」
lines.english: “Ah…”

lines.japanese:
けど、そんなちょっと戸惑い気味の表情は、
まんまとデジカメのデータに変換されてしまった。
lines.english: But before she could hide it, the camera caught that faintly uncertain expression.

lines.japanese:
「お疲れさまでした。
じゃ次、家電コーナー行くぞ」
lines.english: “That’s a wrap. Now let’s head for the appliance department.”

lines.japanese: 「初めての一枚が変装姿かよ…」
lines.english: “So the first picture you take of me is in disguise…”

lines.japanese: 「だって、これはこれで…」
lines.english: “But this has its own…”

lines.japanese: 「…本当に、馬鹿にしやがって」
lines.english: “…You really are making fun of me.”

lines.japanese:
「別に馬鹿になんかしてないって。
本当に似合って…」
lines.english: “I’m not. It genuinely suits you.”

lines.japanese:
「あ…そうだ。
レシート」
lines.english: “Oh, right. The receipt.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　何の？」
lines.english: “What receipt?”

lines.japanese:
「変装道具一式のだよ。
お前、全部現金で払ってたよな？」
lines.english: “For the whole disguise kit. You paid cash for everything, didn’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あ～………そっか」
lines.english: “Oh… Right.”

lines.japanese: ちぇっ、気づかれた。
lines.english: Damn. She had noticed.

lines.japanese:
「後でまとめて精算するから、
とりあえず渡しておいて…」
lines.english: “I’ll reimburse you for everything later. Just give me the receipt for now…”

lines.japanese:
「いるかそんなの。
俺のニーズで買ったんだから」
lines.english: “Forget it. I was the one who wanted them.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
俺が払うためにわざと現金払いにしたのに、
なんて空気を読まない奴だ…
lines.english: I had deliberately paid cash so I could cover it myself. Why did she have to be so incapable of taking a hint?

lines.japanese:
「その代わり、これから買う家電とか家具は別だぞ？
今の買い物と比べて金額の桁が違うしな」
lines.english: “But the furniture and appliances are different. Those are in a completely different price range.”

lines.japanese:
「聞いてるのか？
ちゃんと払えよ？」
lines.english: “Are you listening? You’re paying for those.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ…」
lines.english: “Y-Yeah…”

lines.japanese:
「それならいいんだよ。
さ、今度こそ行くぞ」
lines.english: “Good. Now let’s get moving.”

lines.japanese: 「…春希」
lines.english: “…Haruki.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、それと櫛は後でちゃんと踏んでおけよ？
そうしないと苦しんで死ぬことになるからな」
lines.english: “Oh, and make sure you step on the comb afterward. Otherwise it’s one short step from comb to tomb.”
lines.japaneseRuby:
「あ、それと櫛は後でちゃんと踏んでおけよ？
そうしないと[R苦^９]しんで[R死^４]ぬことになるからな」

lines.japanese: 「現実的なくせに迷信深いなお前は…」
lines.english: “For such a practical man, you’re remarkably superstitious…”

lines.japanese:
こうして、『冬馬かずさ独占取材』の初日は、
何の計画性もなく、唐突にスタートを切った。
lines.english: And so, without warning or anything resembling a plan, the first day of my “Exclusive Interview with Kazusa Touma” began.

lines.japanese:
かずさは、やっぱり悪態をつきながらも、
今度は先に歩き出す俺の後ろを、
三歩離れてしっかりついてきてくれた。
lines.english: Complaining as always, Kazusa still followed exactly three paces behind me.

lines.japanese: 「よし、これでなんとか一通り揃えたかな？」
lines.english: “Right. I think that covers the essentials.”

lines.japanese:
冷蔵庫、テーブル、ベッド、その他諸々。
家電売り場と家具売り場を縦横無尽に走り回り、
たった数時間で１０万以上も散財してしまった。
lines.english: A refrigerator, table, bed, and a dozen other things. After racing back and forth through the appliance and furniture departments, we had spent more than a hundred thousand yen in a matter of hours.

lines.japanese:
まぁ、冬馬家にしてみれば、
この程度の出費、痛くも痒くもないんだろうけど。
lines.english: To the Touma family, an expense like that was probably beneath notice.

lines.japanese:
…なにしろたった一月程度の滞在のために、
敷金礼金合わせて三か月分を払う気前のいい一家だ。
lines.english: After all, they were extravagant enough to pay three months’ rent in deposits and key money for a stay of barely one month.

lines.japanese:
「うわ…もう２時だぞ。
どれだけあたしを引きずり回せば気が済むんだ」
lines.english: “What? It’s already two. How long are you planning to drag me around?”

lines.japanese: 「…文句言うだけの奴は楽でいいよなぁ」
lines.english: “Must be nice when all you do is complain.”

lines.japanese: 結局、店員との交渉は全て俺任せ。
lines.english: Every negotiation with the sales staff had been left to me.

lines.japanese:
かずさは暇そうに店内の商品を見て回り、
最終的な俺の選択にケチをつけるだけ。
lines.english: Kazusa had wandered idly among the merchandise, emerging only to criticize my final choice.

lines.japanese:
「もうちょっとデザインも考慮に入れろ。
春希、お前機能とコストパフォーマンスしか
見てないじゃないか」
lines.english: “You could at least think about the design. All you care about is function and getting the most for your money.”

lines.japanese: 「生活必需品選びにそれ以外の観点があるか？」
lines.english: “What other criteria are there for basic necessities?”

lines.japanese:
「だからお前の生活には潤いが足りないんだ。
もうちょっとゆとりを持って生きろよこの働き蟻」
lines.english: “That’s why there’s no joy in your life. Learn to take it easy, you worker ant.”

lines.japanese: 「お前、自分がキリギリスだって自覚してるだろ？」
lines.english: “You do realize that makes you the grasshopper?”

lines.japanese:
けれど『じゃあどれならいいんだよ？』という
俺の質問に、『そんなの知るか』で返してくるから、
結局最初に選んだのに決まるという展開の繰り返し。
lines.english: Yet whenever I asked which one she wanted instead, she answered, “How should I know?” So we ended up buying my original choice every time.

lines.japanese:
かずさがいちいち文句さえつけなきゃ、
余裕で１時に間に合ってたんだけど。
lines.english: If Kazusa hadn’t objected to every single item, we could easily have finished by one.

lines.japanese:
「とにかく用事はこれで終わりなんだな？
あたしはもう練習に向かっていいんだな？」
lines.english: “Anyway, that’s everything, right? I can finally go practice?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、お疲れさま」
lines.english: “Yeah. Thanks.”

lines.japanese:
「本当に疲れるのはこれからだ…
今から十時間だからな」
lines.english: “The real work starts now. I still have ten hours ahead of me.”

lines.japanese:
「…今日もやるのか？
随分と遅くから始めるのに」
lines.english: “…You’re still doing all ten today? Even starting this late?”

lines.japanese: 「ん…日課だからな」
lines.english: “Mm. It’s my routine.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか…」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese:
なんて、これからの地獄の特訓に
思いを馳せてるはずなのに。
lines.english: She should have been bracing herself for the hellish practice ahead.

lines.japanese:
かずさの表情は昨夜からだんだん…
いや、先週末からどんどん穏やかになってきてる。
lines.english: Kazusa’s expression had been growing calmer since last night… No, it had been softening more and more since last weekend.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、春希…」
lines.english: “Well, then, Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あのさ…
できれば弾いてるところも撮らせてくれないかな？」
lines.english: “Actually… would you let me photograph you playing?”

lines.japanese:
「悪い…練習だけは見せたくないんだ。
まだ仕上がってないから」
lines.english: “Sorry. I don’t want you watching me practice. My playing isn’t ready yet.”

lines.japanese:
「最初の数分だけでいいんだけどな。
その、弾いてるふりしてくれれば」
lines.english: “I only need a few minutes. You could just pretend to play.”

lines.japanese:
「コンサートの後にしてくれ。
今は集中したいんだ」
lines.english: “Wait until after the concert. I need to concentrate now.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか…ごめん、無理言って」
lines.english: “I see… Sorry for pushing.”

lines.japanese: 「いや…あたしの方こそ」
lines.english: “No… I’m the one who should apologize.”

lines.japanese:
その証拠に、
以前なら怒鳴られてもおかしくないやり取りも、
こうしてお互い譲歩しあうことができる。
lines.english: That was proof enough of how she had changed. A conversation that once might have ended with her screaming at me could now end with each of us giving a little.

lines.japanese:
「じゃ、頑張ってな。
そうだ、晩飯はどうする？」
lines.english: “Good luck, then. Oh—what do you want to do about dinner?”

lines.japanese:
「なんでもいい。
どうせ何作っても大して美味くないだろ、お前」
lines.english: “Anything. Whatever you make, it won’t be very good.”

lines.japanese: 「………わかったよ」
lines.english: “…Fine.”

lines.japanese:
そのかずさの答えを受けた俺の苦笑いは、
とっくに背中を向けたかずさには
届いていなかったかもしれない。
lines.english: Kazusa had already turned away, so she may never have seen the rueful smile her answer drew from me.

lines.japanese:
本当は『外で済ませてくるか家で食うか』を
聞いたつもりだったんだけどな…
lines.english: I’d only meant to ask whether she wanted to eat out or have dinner at home…

lines.japanese: 「今は無理に決まってるだろ、春希…」
lines.english: “Of course I can’t show you now, Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
「だってさ…
お前に最高の冬馬かずさを見せるためだけに、
あたしは日本まで来たんだぞ？」
lines.english: “I came all the way to Japan for one reason—to show you Kazusa Touma at her very best.”
